text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- State security sacked head of Kaunas department on suspicions of suppressing the information provided by volunteer force head Juras Abromavicius about who was responsible for blowing up the Brazuole river railway bridge three years ago.
- Prosecutors are demanding a 10-year prison sentence for the suspected leader of Kaunas gangland Henrikas Daktaras. The verdict is expected on February 13.
- Bank of Lithuania governor says litas will remain stabile even after the currency board system is abolished.

- Vilnius prosecutor's office has put an arrest on the apartment of the former Finance Minister Rolandas Matiliauskas, sacked after a bank loan row. Matliauskas will face questioning in the near future, the newspaper says.
- Central bank governor says the banking sector is regaining confidence after 1995 crisis.
- The birth rate in Lithuania is increases among teenagers only. Some 50 teenage marriages were registered in Vilnius in 1996.

- The prime ministers of the three Baltic countries discussed in Tallinn a free trade agreement with agricultural products, a customs union and the co-operation in the integration into European Union.
- Lithuania's dependence on Russian gas will last a long time, the newspaper writes. Lithuanian Gas owes the Russian gas suppliers $34 million.
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius says he has three finance minister candidates but refuses to name them. Meanwhile the state budget was 200 million litas short in January.
- China state owned Qing Qi company intends to invest $2.25 million in problem-ridden Siauliai Vairas bicycle producer and buy up to a 90 percent stake.
- The Lithuanian government has included 842 companies, worth 1.2 billion litas, into the privatisation list for 1997.
- Some 5,800 new cars were sold in Lithuania in 1996 and 2,216 of them have remained in the country.
